{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "AJCR.w4-rep",
      "title": "Wave 4: representability of Pic^0 (curve-specialised Kleiman)",
      "projects": [
        "Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild"
      ],
      "summary": "================================================================================
CURRENT STATE, READ THIS FIRST (review-ajcr r4, 2026-07-30). Everything below
this block is the audit HISTORY: five layers of correction and self-correction,
in which the actual costing does not appear until roughly halfway down. It is
kept because each retraction is evidence, but a lane picking a target should
read this block and then jump to the header "THE COSTING, RE-RANKED".
================================================================================

THE MACHINE IS SOUND AND HAS NOTHING TO FEED IT. pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) and mixedParamRepresentableBy
(Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) are sorry-free, kernel-confirmed, non-circular,
and WOULD produce a representing scheme. All three antecedents are undischarged
and no sorry-free witness exists for any of them.

THE THREE ANTECEDENTS, ranked by measured cost, cheapest last:
 1. IsChartUniv (the per-index chart certificate, `hf`) -- CERT-Sigma-gated.
    Refuted at V = top and free-but-useless at V = bot; whether the PAIR holds at
    any V strictly between is UNMEASURED at every V. Inhabitation at one concrete
    V is the open question. Rows: chart-u, chart-restrict, atlas-coupling.
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc f (DAT-B coverage) -- the most
    expensive, and multi-round (told to the human as I-1090). Cannot be discounted
    by restricting the atlas: ajcr-p1's isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono carries
    any V up to top, where the inclusion is an iso. Restricted coverage is no
    cheaper than unrestricted -- and note only ONE direction is proved, so it is
    as measured STRICTLY STRONGER. Row: dat-b.
 3. rep i (a representation of divFunctor at each parameter) -- the divisor-
    representability lane's target. Rows: ddr.divrep (+ u2, abel-widened).

RIDERS THAT ARE NOT SEPARATE OBLIGATIONS, both established by retraction below:
 * hD (LocallyOfFiniteType) is a rider on antecedent 3, proved via
   rep.uniqueUpToIso -- unconditional, not contingent on the carrier divRep
   returns.
 * hcpt IS the JacobianData.quasiCompact field, so dat-glue and dat-j name ONE
   obligation. Qualification (r4, I-1162): the half carrying that -- the mpr
   direction -- has been the producer's own implementation since 07-27
   (JacobianDataCharts.lean:216); the new content is the mp direction, which
   shows the identification cannot be undone. hcl still has no producer, so
   nothing there is discharged.

r4 REPRICING -- WITHDRAWN BY ITS AUTHOR, same session. I wrote here that the chart
parameter n is pinned to the genus by chi_moduleKSheaf UNCONDITIONALLY, so
abel-noninj owed no "we are at n = g" argument and its n > g branch was
unreachable. FALSE, refuted by a fresh-context audit (I-1176) and reproduced:
chi_moduleKSheaf CONVERTS chi = 1 - n into n = genus C, it does not SUPPLY
chi = 1 - n. With n free and no chi hypothesis the goal FAILS, and it still fails
with a representation at n in scope. My probe had hchi as a binder, so it measured
the conversion (I-1177).
   THE STANDING PRICE is ajcr-p2's: n > g is unreachable for a chart built on a
producer IN THIS TREE, because each such producer carries an hchi at its own
index. That is a claim about producers and a lane must keep them in view.
Whether an inhabitant exists at n != genus C is an OPEN inhabitation question
about DivRepAffinePullback -- mixedParamChart typechecks at arbitrary nn.
abel-noninj's live target is unchanged: the carve question, does DivScheme g
contain points where H^1 fails to vanish.

SORRY COUNT IS NOT DEBT HERE: 17 sorries, all in Challenge.lean (15, the
statement-only north star) and Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean (2). A naive count reads
AJCR as nearly done. It is not -- the gap is the three antecedents above, none of
which is a sorry.

ANSWER TO THE COSTING QUESTION, unchanged this round: none of the three closes
this week (human-facing accounting at I-0984). The items where a single round can
still produce a DECISIVE result rather than partial progress are antecedent 1's
inhabitation at one concrete V, and the abel-noninj carve question now that its
degree is pinned.

================================================================================
HISTORY FOLLOWS -- corrections in reverse chronological layers.
================================================================================

*** hcpt CLAUSE RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), refuted by ajcr-p4 (I-1007)
within minutes of my writing it. THE DEGENERACY OBSERVATION IS REAL; MY CAUSAL READING WAS
CONFOUNDED. ***

I wrote, in the self-correction below, that "hcpt is NOT an independent gate but a CONSEQUENCE of
coverage", inferred from hcpt being free at iota := PEmpty while all content sat in the
IsLocallySurjective instance. p4's refutation is decisive and I verified its pivot myself (EXIT=0):
PEmpty IS FINITE. So freeness of hcpt there is explained by the FINITE-INDEX route
(JacobianData.ofCharts with per-chart compactness at an empty cover), with coverage contributing
nothing. A degenerate index attributes to whichever hypothesis happens to vary, and I varied the
wrong one.

WHAT p4 MEASURED, more useful than my claim was: feeding the openCover route directly,
(glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace fails on EXACTLY ONE goal --
Finite (glueData hf).openCover.I0. Not chart compactness, not the cover being a cover, not
coverage. Add [Finite iota] plus per-chart CompactSpace and the same term closes. p4 also applies my
own I-0978 correctly: a failing synthesis measures the instance graph, so this does NOT prove hcpt
independent of coverage -- it shows no route in scope derives it, and the single gap on the
available route is INDEX FINITENESS, which the class-indexed atlas provably lacks.

CONSEQUENCE, and it strengthens the item rather than weakening it: DO NOT schedule "derive hcpt
from coverage". The two honest options are the ones the tree names -- a finite atlas, or the Abel
image (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage out of a quasi-compact DivScheme). The class-indexed atlas
needs the second, and PRICING IT is the unowned work. Row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j points there.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006, after a fresh-context
review of my OWN correction below). THE FOURTH ITEM IS NOT AN ANTECEDENT AT ALL -- IT IS A RIDER
ON antecedent 3, AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN ARGUED IT. Read this before the arithmetic
correction that follows; that correction's CONCLUSION survives but its UNIT OF PRICING was wrong. ***

WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WHAT I GOT WRONG. Right: the count was 3-of-3 where the goal needs more, the
"derived, not assumed" sentence was misleading, and ajcr-p4's discharge is real. WRONG: I priced
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom as a FOURTH INDEPENDENT ANTECEDENT that p4 removed,
and justified its cheapness by the CARRIER the divRep lane happens to return today
(locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom). That argument is CONTINGENT -- it would need re-measuring
if divRep ever returned a different object.

THE UNCONDITIONAL FACT, PROBED, `lake env lean` EXIT=0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound]: if divFunctor C pi n is representable by D and by D', and D'.hom is locally of finite
type, then D.hom is. Three lines -- e := rep.uniqueUpToIso rep', e.hom.left is IsIso via
Over.comp_left on hom_inv_id, then rw [<- Over.w e.hom] and infer_instance.

SO hD IS AN INVARIANT OF THE FUNCTOR AT THE PARAMETER, not a property of the chosen carrier. No
producer of rep can choose a D that fails it, and none can be blamed for one that does. The right
place for it on this board is as a RIDER ON THE rep ROW (divrep), not as an item of its own -- a
row that lists it separately INFLATES the antecedent count, which is the same error in the
opposite direction from the one I was correcting.

THE ANTECEDENT LIST OF THE GOAL, corrected again and now on unconditional grounds:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability -- CARRYING hD as a rider that costs its producer nothing.
    OPEN (divrep.u2).
 4. quasiCompact. OPEN, and see the degeneracy note below, which reprices it.

AND A DEGENERACY THAT REPRICES quasiCompact, measured on the same pass. At iota := PEmpty EVERY
explicit input of jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts is free -- hf/hdeg/V/hD/m/Z/nn by PEmpty.elim,
and hcpt free too because an empty family glues to an EMPTY space (IsEmpty => CompactSpace by
inferInstance). ALL the content sits in the single IsLocallySurjective instance. The output is
nevertheless NOT vacuous, and that was also probed (EXIT=0, same axioms): that instance at PEmpty
implies False, because JacobianData.rep yields a point of J over every test (homEquiv.symm 1)
while J.left is empty. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (a) the assembly is sound and falsifiable, so nothing
here is a HasDivFunctor-style vacuity; (b) hcpt is NOT an independent gate of this shape but a
CONSEQUENCE of coverage -- and any future "hcpt discharged" measured at a small atlas measures
nothing at all.

ALSO CORRECTED, and it is a false absolute I repeated from p4's file: "the only declaration in
Picard/ whose conclusion is LocallyOfFiniteType is locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom". There are FIVE
non-local ones plus 38 local re-derivations; the omitted ones include the very instance
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199) that Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean imports and cites to make hD free, so the
absolute is refuted by that file's own closing section. THE DEFENSIBLE FORM, which is what a board
row should say: no producer AT A CHART. Same absolute is live on row
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.atlas-lft ("exactly ONE declaration") -- narrow it there too.

*** ARITHMETIC CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006). THE ANTECEDENT COUNT ON THIS
ROW WAS THREE-OF-THREE WHERE THE GOAL NEEDS FOUR-OF-FOUR, AND ONE SENTENCE BELOW IS MISLEADING
IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. Audited ajcr-p4's finding (I-0967/I-0977); it is CORRECT. ***

THE SENTENCE TO FIX IS MINE. Below, this row says the big-site sheaf condition, the 01JJ gluing
and "BOTH finiteness certificates -- which are DERIVED from chart-level hypotheses, not assumed"
are done and kernel-checked. Read against the statements that is wrong in effect: they are derived
from chart-level hypotheses THAT NOTHING IN THE TREE PRODUCED, which is not the same as derived.
locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (JacobianDataCharts.lean:154) TAKES
hlft : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i); it was, until 67c8d24d5, the only Picard/
declaration concluding LocallyOfFiniteType at a chart, so the certificate was an assumption on
every route. PicRepDatum.lft (PicRepDatum.lean:100) is a structure FIELD -- also an assumption --
and toJacobianData (JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:87) only carries it across. So a lane that
discharged all THREE tracked antecedents would NOT have produced a JacobianData C, which is what
Challenge.lean's frozen Jacobian := (jacobianData C).J actually needs.

NOW DISCHARGED, AND IT IS A REAL DISCHARGE RATHER THAN A RELOCATION -- the part I checked hardest,
because "reduces to X" usually just moves the bill. Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean (ajcr-p4) proves
locallyOfFiniteType_chartHom_mixedParamChart: at the REAL atlas the certificate follows from
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom alone. And hD is FREE at the carrier the
divisor-representability lane returns: PROBED, imports current, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 --
LocallyOfFiniteType (divSchemeOver k A B g r1 r2 b1 b2).hom closes by inferInstance ALONE at
ARBITRARY window data, via the global instance locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199), and DivOver (DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:113-116, :308) is an instance of
exactly that shape. So a lane producing rep supplies the fourth antecedent at the same moment at
zero cost.

WHAT REPLACES THE THREE-ITEM LIST, as the antecedent list of the GOAL:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability. OPEN (divrep.u2, ajcr-p3).
 4. hlft, chart finiteness. DISCHARGED at the real atlas, free at the rep carrier.
 5. quasiCompact. OPEN and GENUINELY A-POSTERIORI, and this is the item to watch now that 4 is
    gone. PER-CHART compactness is free at the same carrier (compactSpace_divScheme); CompactSpace
    of the GLUED object is not, and for the class-indexed (infinite) atlas the finite route
    JacobianData.ofCharts is unavailable, so it must come from the Abel image
    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage). Do not let the freeness of the per-chart form be quoted
    for the glued form -- that conflation is exactly what this correction is about.

THE VERDICT IS UNCHANGED: none of the three OPEN antecedents closes this week (I-0873). Item 4
was never on the list, so removing it does not shorten the critical path; what it does is make
the remaining list the true one. One caveat on the discharging file itself:
Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean:65 claims "everything in it other than hf, the local-surjectivity
instance and rep is now discharged", while hcpt is an explicit hypothesis of the same definition
and the file's own :184-186 and :262-265 call it open. The :262 reading is the correct one.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0004, after a fresh-context
review of my own work). THE IsPlusHonest FINDING BELOW IS OVERSTATED ON THE STEP THAT CARRIES IT.
The route-decision conclusion SURVIVES, for a different and better-evidenced reason. ***

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I argued: relPicToPicEt lands in PicEtAff.unit, unit is mk at the TRIVIAL cover
`.self A` alone, therefore honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed. That step is
FALSE. PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean:48) proves a unit class is presented on
EVERY cover E, not only on `.self` -- so "mk at the trivial cover" describes one PRESENTATION, not
the RANGE, and nothing follows about which classes the range contains.

AND THE ABSOLUTE FORM IS REFUTED BY A LANDED THEOREM IN THIS TREE:
PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141) proves the unit SURJECTIVE
over a field test K admitting a curve point sigma, upgraded to a MulEquiv by
PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (:186). Over such tests honesty is DISCHARGED OUTRIGHT -- vacuously
true, no etale cover needed anywhere. So "IsPlusHonest is the sheafification gap asserted of an
arbitrary section" is wrong as an absolute.

THE CORRECTED CLAIM, which is narrower and better supported. The gap is at a GENERAL AFFINE BASE
WITH NO SECTION, and the tree documents exactly why:
 * the field route closes only through etale-cover cofinality in finite separable field extensions
   (Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom, EtaleCover.lean:287) -- there is NO
   general-base analogue of that cofinality;
 * EffectivityMoving.lean:41-48 states plainly that for a merely quasi-finite (non-finite) etale
   cover the moving statement is FALSE, with a counterexample sketch (B = A_u x A_v over a
   2-dimensional normal local A with nontrivial local class group). So the [Module.Finite A B]
   hypothesis in the effectivity layer is load-bearing, not convenience.

SO THE OBSTRUCTION IS BASE-SHAPE, NOT ARBITRARINESS OF THE CLASS. Two consequences:
 1. the split to hand a prover lane is NOT "chart value (cheap) vs arbitrary section (blocked)" but
    "field test with a section (FREE) vs general sectionless affine base (OPEN)". The delta between
    the chart side and the coverage side is NARROWER than I priced it;
 2. antecedent 2 still owes a route decision -- which site coverage is local for -- because the
    repair still refines covers and descends, and Zariski-local surjectivity still will not absorb
    that. The conclusion stands; cite the module-finiteness counterexample, NOT the trivial-cover
    claim, when repeating it.

Also corrected, same review: I called DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean UNROOTED. It is ROOTED --
AlgebraicJacobian.lean:346 imports it at HEAD (commit 2b8cef366) and its .olean exists, so it IS
kernel-checked. Another lane rooted it while I was auditing it and I did not re-run the grep before
publishing. I-0941's step (i) is therefore already done; its step (ii) stands.

--- the original finding follows; read its trivial-cover reasoning as retracted ---

*** RANKING AMENDMENT, second reviewer pass 2026-07-29 (run 0082 session 0004, review-ajcr).
ANTECEDENT 2 IS NOT A GEOMETRY BILL, IT IS A SITE DECISION -- so the #2 slot below is
MIS-JUSTIFIED even though its position may be right. Issue I-0920. ***

The costing below is otherwise intact and should be read as it stands. This amendment changes ONE
thing: the reason antecedent 2 (dat-b B-5/B-6, local surjectivity) is expensive.

BELOW IT SAYS: "It carries the content, and its packaging is complete ... What it owes is geometry:
the per-point datum, plus the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation."

MEASURED, tracing the per-point datum through its own producer chain rather than through the rows'
prose. The producer exists (exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range, rooted, sorry-free), and what
it needs reduces to ONE hypothesis: IsPlusHonest (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200). Read as a
statement, that says: for every affine open U of the test, the class restricted to U lies in the
RANGE of relPicToPicEt -- i.e. Zariski-locally the class comes from the UN-sheafified relPic.

That is the etale-sheafification gap, structurally:
 * picEt is built on PicEtAff (PicEt.lean:9-21), and PicEtAff C A (PicEtAff.lean:218) is a QUOTIENT
   OVER ALL ETALE COVERS -- elements are PicEtAff.mk E x;
 * PicEtAff.unit (:377), the target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126), is mk at the TRIVIAL
   cover `.self A` alone.
So honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed on that piece -- precisely what the
one-step plus construction exists to permit to FAIL. The tree's only honesty mechanism agrees:
Pic0ChartHonest.lean's own "does not give" says honesty holds over Spec E.Carrier and NOT over
Spec A, bought by CHANGING THE BASE, with "Nothing here performs that descent".

WHY THE CHART SIDE IS UNAFFECTED, which is what makes this a real distinction rather than a blanket
pessimism: chartValue = abelDiv * sigmaFamily * (thetaFamily^m)^{-1} (DivSchemeAbel.lean:351, read
from the definition), and honesty is discharged for each factor and closed under the group
operations. Coverage is different because chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise
(Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) quantifies over EVERY s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T);
arbitrariness is the content of coverage, and narrowing s to chart-value shape makes it circular.

CONSEQUENCE. Antecedent 2 splits into a cheap half and an out-of-reach half, and the rows conflate
them: honesty of coverage's own WITNESS is already covered; honesty of the class coverage must HIT
is the gap. The repair -- refine to the etale carrier, then descend -- changes the site from Zariski
to etale, and pic0RepresentableByOfCharts' antecedent is Zariski-local surjectivity. No leaf settles
that. It is a route question for the human/reviewer layer, and it is the third antecedent-level
obstruction found on this seam after the unrestricted-certificate fork (antecedent 1) and U2.

NOT A REFUTATION. Proving IsPlusHonest false for an arbitrary class needs a class not
Zariski-locally in relPic's image; this tree has no Brauer or nontrivial-etale-class machinery to
build one, and I did not build it. The claim is the weaker sufficient one: it is not a lemma about
the tree's own constructions, and a lane sent at it will not find a proof.

THE VERDICT BELOW ("none of the three antecedents closes this week") is unchanged and, if anything,
better supported: the antecedent that looked closest to being a bounded geometry bill is the one
that turns out to need a decision above the leaf layer.

--- the first reviewer pass's costing follows, accurate except as amended above ---

*** THE COSTING, RE-RANKED 2026-07-29 (run 0082, review-ajcr). THE THREE ANTECEDENTS ARE NOT THREE
INDEPENDENT PRICES, AND NONE OF THEM CLOSES THIS WEEK. Read this before picking a leaf. ***

WHAT IS GENUINELY SOUND, and it is worth stating first because it is unusual: pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) and mixedParamRepresentableBy (Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) are
sorry-free, rooted, and honest. Given the three antecedents they WOULD produce a representing scheme.
The machine is correct. Nothing feeds it.

THE THREE ANTECEDENTS DO NOT COMPOSE AS THE ROWS IMPLY. Measured, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 (probes in
run 0082 session dir /probes):
 (1) `hf` = IsChartUniv (Pic0ChartPair.lean:173) is stated at a FREE `V : D.left.Opens`. At ι = PEmpty
     the whole seam call elaborates with `hf := fun i => PEmpty.elim i` -- no charts, no rep, no
     IsChartUniv. At V = bottom, injectivity is free (no nonempty test has a point of the empty open).
     So `hf` at an arbitrary V carries NO CONTENT.
     QUALIFIED by ajcr-p1 (I-0890), correctly: 'free at V = bottom' is true of the INJECTIVITY clause
     and of exists_factor, and FALSE of the fibre DATUM -- its sq field at an empty test needs
     Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C ..) over an empty base, which is true, separate, and absent from the
     tree. So the degenerate value shows a clause is cheap without exhibiting an inhabitant: CHEAP and
     SATISFIABLE come apart, and several rows on this leaf have been priced by exactly that
     conflation. The ι = PEmpty conclusion below is unaffected -- it never used V = bottom.
 (2) The seam is nonetheless NOT vacuous: at ι = PEmpty the sup sieve is BOTTOM, and the bottom sieve
     is Zariski-covering only for an EMPTY test. So ALL the content forcing the atlas to be an atlas
     sits in the LOCAL-SURJECTIVITY instance -- antecedent 2, not antecedent 1.
 (3) THE UNPRICED OBLIGATION, which no row owned before this pass: coverage
     (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise, Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) must produce
     `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ X i`, i.e. INTO `(V i : Scheme)`. So coverage must hit the SAME V at which
     `hf` was certified. chartLocus is an open of the TEST; V is an open of the DIVISOR SCHEME. Zero
     files in the tree mention both IsChartUniv and ChartsCoverLocally. Now owned by
     AJCR.w4-rep.datum.chart-restrict (ajcr-p1, I-0869/I-0872).

WORSE, AND INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED WITH ajcr-p1: the only non-circular producer of `hf`,
isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre (Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:170), goes THROUGH the unrestricted
certificate -- its body is `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` with the restriction
applied afterwards. So IsChartLocusFibre implies IsOpenImmersion.presheaf of the UNRESTRICTED Abel
chart, which three headers call false (|D| is not a point). QUALIFICATION I add: that falsity is a
HEADER CLAIM, unproved -- isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective
(Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:219) takes non-injectivity as a HYPOTHESIS and is never
instantiated. So the tree holds a reduction and its conditional refutation and has connected neither.

THE RANKING, corrected. Not by ease -- by what a discharge would actually buy:
 1. chart-restrict (the V-coupling + a fibre criterion at the RESTRICTED chart). Held by ajcr-p1.
    Without it antecedents 1 and 2 cannot be composed at all, so it outranks both.
 2. Antecedent 2, local surjectivity (dat-b B-5/B-6). It carries the content, and its packaging is
    complete: isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise takes B-5 to the instance in ONE step, with
    a converse, so the pointwise form is not a strengthening chosen to be provable. What it owes is
    geometry: the per-point datum, plus the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation.
 3. Antecedent 1, `hf`. Real but currently unreachable except through the unrestricted statement.
 4. Antecedent 3, `rep i` (divrep/u2). Multi-round: U2 is refuted on the widened route
    (isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling), and the live question is a chart-free eps-value.

RE-PRICED LEAVES, both directions, all verified by reading the Lean rather than the prose:
 * OVER-PRICED (I-0870): dat-b, chart-u and c9b all say the per-affine-piece datum has NO PRODUCER.
   It has one -- exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:178),
   rooted and sorry-free, with chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest (:334) giving c9b clause (i) as DATA and
   haff DISCHARGED. Residue is IsPlusHonest at the coverage class, which is narrower.
 * MIS-ROUTED (I-0862): the rejection cluster's forwarding address, twist-atlas, is the GL_2(k) route
   protection I-0492 FORBIDS (twistedP1Map = pi >> P1.autOfMatrix). Now rejected. The four rejections
   themselves are each CORRECT, and three of them are ONE fact -- pieces confined to a fixed chart
   pair -- which R2 already removed.
 * dat-glue: unchanged and correctly deferred; it consumes the above.

VERDICT TO THE HUMAN (also sent --to human): none of the three antecedents closes this week. The
reachable wins this round are the coupling statement and the re-pricings, not a discharge.

BUILD REACHABILITY IS FIXED, and the paragraph near the end of this row saying otherwise is STALE:
93/620 unrooted is now 18/756, the entire DD-R tail is rooted, and the 18 remaining are essentially
the old triage's own DELETE list plus Pic0ThetaCocycle. See AJCR.w4-rep.build-reach. Exactly 17 code
sorries project-wide: Challenge.lean 15 (the statement-only north star) and Pic0ThetaCocycle 2

THE ANSWER.  R1 -- varying the pinned pair of P^1-points per cover member, i.e. the p1-aut ->
fibre-avoid -> cert-relocalize chain -- is correct IF AND ONLY IF |P^1(k)| >= n + 2, where n is

and s in W_c iff the FIBRE supp(D_s) meets pi^{-1}(c).  Since D_s is finite of degree n over
kappa(s), its image in |P^1| has at most n closed points.
  IF: pick c in P^1(k) outside that image and any c' /= c; then Spec R minus W_c confines D to the
  chart complementary to pi^{-1}(c).  Doing this at every s gives a Zariski cover on which the
  divisor is confined, with the pair varying per member -- exactly what R1 allows.
  ONLY IF: if the sum over c in P^1(k) of e_c is at most n, where e_c is the minimal degree of a
  closed point of C over c, then a divisor of the form sum_c q_c + padding lies in W_c for EVERY
  c in P^1(k), and no pinned pair confines it.

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.

Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain

  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it

`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those

shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean

  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").

  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

name: horizon-inbox
description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.

Read in this order before editing:

1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every
   active protection is required even if your team previously marked it read.
2. `horizon inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json` — open each
   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read
   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.
3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.

The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
it explicitly.

## Act

Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
UI); you do not pass this yourself.

New inbox items use a two-part body:

- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
  item that is only a title is rejected.

Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Operational
messages are deltas, not reports. Default to one sentence or at most three short
bullets covering conclusion, new evidence, and next action; do not repeat the
thread, commit diff, or session history. Use headings only when a genuinely
multi-part decision needs them. Agent comments target at most 600 characters and
are rejected above 1200; descriptions/opening messages target 800 and are
rejected above 2400. Humans are not subject to these bounds.

Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
of that paragraph concise.

Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.

### Conversation lifecycle

A conversation is for an expected reply, decision, or active coordination. A
one-way handoff or announcement is an `info`/`hint`, not a conversation.

1. **Search before starting:** inspect open conversations for the same topic and
   participants (`inbox list --status open --kind conversation --query "key words"
   --json`). Reply to the existing thread whenever it can carry the update. Do not
   open one thread per incremental finding.
2. **One question, one thread:** keep follow-ups, answers, corrections, and the
   final decision as comments on that thread. Start another only when it has a
   genuinely different decision boundary or participant set.
3. **Answer before branching:** when a conversation becomes unread, open it and
   answer or acknowledge it before starting another conversation with the same
   team.
4. **The initiator closes:** if `metadata.started_by` is your task/run, you own
   the lifecycle. Once the requested answer has arrived and been consumed, add a
   short conclusion comment when the outcome is not obvious, then
   `horizon inbox archive <id>`. Do this during the session, not only after a
   warning says the inbox is full.
5. **Do not hide an answer from its initiator:** recipients normally reply and
   leave closure to the initiator. For a human-started thread, answer it but leave
   it open for the human to consume/archive unless the human explicitly delegates
   closure. Use `complete` instead of `archive` only when the concluded thread is
   intentionally meant to remain visible in the resolved working record.
6. **End-of-session sweep:** before the final report, inspect open conversations
   in which your task is `started_by`. Archive every resolved one and state a real
   blocker on any that must remain open. An accumulation of open conversations is
   unfinished coordination, not harmless history.

- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body "..."` — progress note on an item (record
  what changed; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name
  into the body; authorship is automatic. Comment only at a **key advance** such
  as a milestone, ruled-out route, blocker, correction, or conclusion. Update the
  existing thread with the delta instead of re-establishing its full context.
- `horizon inbox dm task:<id> [task:<id> ...] --body "Topic\n\nOpening message"`
  — start a one-to-one or group conversation. Use `horizon ps` to discover live
  teams. Use it only after the lifecycle search above. The sender remains a
  participant and owns closure; every reply makes the thread unread for the other
  participants. Humans read and reply from the live dashboard.
- **Write comments as mathematics, for a human.** State the key step that
  succeeded in human-readable mathematical language (LaTeX for formulas), naming
  the result and the idea — e.g. "Proved $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})=0$ for $i>\dim X$ by
  reducing to the affine case via Čech cohomology." Mention Lean declaration
  names and file paths only as supporting detail; the substance is the maths, not
  a code changelog. This applies to comments on **roadmap items and tasks** too:
  when a key step lands, record it there in the same mathematical, legible style.
- `horizon inbox archive <id>` — soft-delete: keep the item for the record but
  hide it from the dashboard by default. Use for stale, superseded, consumed, or
  no-longer-key context. Keeping the inbox tidy this way is your job (or the
  janitor subagent's) — prune memory/info so they remain small.

  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).

    tag to the body.
  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,
    so it stays invisible to agents until a human releases it.

name: horizon-start
description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
---

Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
ago, and their report was written for you.

This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
tenth of the session.

## The four signals

```bash
ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
```

The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
like:

```
0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
0003-system
0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
```

For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:

- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
  single most informative bit on disk.
- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
  four minutes ago or last week.

## Which situation am I in?

Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.

**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.

**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
ledger.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
tried and rejected.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
stand before proposing work.

One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
the run's original plan.)

## Then, before you start

- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
  `horizon-inbox`.

Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
here.

All rights reserved.\n3\tReleased under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.\n4\tAuthors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors\n5\t-/\n6\timport AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SupportTube\n7\timport Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Finite\n8\t\n9\t/-!\n10\t# The support-tube finiteness engine: the (c1)-finite production brick (G-4)\n11\t\n12\tThe algebraic half of the DDR-4 certificate clause (c1) (`informal/w4-g4-worksheet.md`\n13\t\u00a73, the one row with no landed engine): for a divisor adaptation over a test ring `R`,\n14\tthe chart-local colength `\u0393(D(h_j)) \u29f8 (f_j)` is a **finite** `R`-module \u2014 Kleiman's\n15\tfiniteness-of-the-divisor-subscheme step, per piece.\n16\t\n17\t## The honest hypothesis (probe finding)\n18\t\n19\tThe colength is the section ring of the piece trace of the family support\n20\t(`supportLocus_inter_pieces`): the closed subscheme of the affine piece `D(h_j)` cut by\n21\t`f_j`, whose underlying set is `D(h_j) \\ D(f_j) = supportLocus \u2229 D(h_j)`.  The engine\n22\tinput is that this trace is **closed in the whole relative curve**; universal closedness\n23\tof the curve over the base (the landed licence `instIsProperRelCurveHom`) then makes the\n24\ttrace universally closed over `Spec R`, and a universally closed affine morphism of\n25\tfinite type is finite (`IsIntegralHom.iff_universallyClosed_and_isAffineHom` +\n26\t`IsFinite.iff_isIntegralHom_and_locallyOfFiniteType` \u2014 the mathlib heart, the\n27\t`SlicingFlatKernel` luck again).  No Noetherian hypothesis anywhere.\n28\t\n29\tFibrewise finiteness data alone (each fibre colength artinian, even of constant total\n30\tdimension) canNOT replace the closed-trace input.  Guard examples:\n31\t\n32\t* `\u0393(\ud835\udd38\u00b9) = k[x]` over `k` with `f = 0`: excluded by `[UniversallyClosed]` on the\n33\t  structure morphism (the affine line is not proper).\n34\t* the hyperbola `k[t,x]\u29f8(tx\u22121)` over `k[t]` inside `X = \u2119\u00b9_{k[t]}`, piece the affine\n35\t  chart: every fibre colength is artinian, the module is even flat, yet not finite \u2014\n36\t  the closure of the trace leaks into `(\u221e, t=0)`, so the closed-trace hypothesis fails\n37\t  exactly where it must.\n38\t* two disjoint base sections with a piece missing one point of one section: piece\n39\t  colength `k[t] \u00d7 k[t,t\u207b\u00b9]`, all fibre colengths artinian of constant total dimension\n40\t  `2` on the glued module \u2014 the PER-PIECE trace leaks.  Hence the certificate's\n41\t  per-piece clause genuinely constrains the adaptation, and the fibrewise input of\n42\t  P-fib-N enters this brick only through its topological shadow, the **no-leak fibre\n43\t  criterion** threaded below (`hfib` of\n44\t  `finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset`).\n45\t\n46\t## Main declarations\n47\t\n48\t* `Scheme.LocalEquations.supportLeak` \u2014 the leak locus of a support trace out of an\n49\t  open `U`: `closure (supportLocus \u2229 U) \\ U`, closed\n50\t  (`isClosed_supportLeak`), with `isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`\n51\t  and the fibre criterion `supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre`;\n52\t* `Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_image_supportLeak` \u2014 the tube-side product: the base\n53\t  image of the leak locus is closed under a universally closed structure morphism, so\n54\t  its complement is the Zariski-open base locus where the trace is closed;\n55\t* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.finite_quotient_span_singleton_of_isClosed` \u2014 **the\n56\t  abstract engine**: `V` affine open in `X` over `Spec R`, structure morphism\n57\t  universally closed and locally of finite type, `V \\ D(g)` closed in `X` \u27f9\n58\t  `\u0393(X, V) \u29f8 (g)` is a finite `R`-module (via the closed immersion\n59\t  `Spec (\u0393(X, V) \u29f8 (g)) \u27f6 X` and mathlib's integral = universally closed + affine);\n60\t* `DivisorAdaptation.finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter` /\n61\t  `finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty` /\n62\t  `finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset` /\n63\t  `finite_colength_of_supportLocus_subset` \u2014 **the (c1)-finite clause** for the piece\n64\t  `j`, in the closed-trace, leak-locus, fibrewise no-leak, and dominant-piece\n65\t  spellings.  CertUniv consumes the fibrewise form with `hfib` produced from the seed\n66\t  design + P-fib-N fibre data, or the closed-trace form directly.\n67\t\n68\tThe `R`-algebra structure on section rings is `Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` through the\n69\t`Over` structure (LOCAL instances, house rule) \u2014 consumers must activate the same\n70\tinstances.\n71\t-/\n72\t\n73\tset_option autoImplicit false\n74\t\n75\tuniverse u\n76\t\n77\topen CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite\n78\t\n79\tnamespace AlgebraicGeometry\n80\t\n81\tattribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra\n82\t\n83\t/-! ## The leak locus of a support trace -/\n84\t\n85\tnamespace Scheme.LocalEquations\n86\t\n87\tvariable {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : X.LocalEquations)\n88\t\n89\t/-- **The leak locus of a support trace**: the part of the closure of\n90\t`supportLocus \u2229 U` that escapes `U`.  The trace `supportLocus \u2229 U` is closed in `X`\n91\tiff the leak locus is empty (`isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`);\n92\tits base image under a universally closed structure morphism is closed\n93\t(`isClosed_image_supportLeak`), so the trace is closed over the complementary base\n94\topen \u2014 the Zariski-local piece-isolation mechanism of the DDR-4 finiteness input. -/\n95\tdef supportLeak (U : X.Opens) : Set X :=\n96\t  closure (d.supportLocus \u2229 (U : Set X)) \\ (U : Set X)\n97\t\n98\tlemma isClosed_supportLeak (U : X.Opens) : IsClosed (d.supportLeak U) :=\n99\t  isClosed_closure.sdiff U.isOpen\n100\t\n101\t/-- The leak locus lies in the support outside the open: leaks are support points. -/\n102\tlemma supportLeak_subset_sdiff (U : X.Opens) :\n103\t    d.supportLeak U \u2286 d.supportLocus \\ (U : Set X) := fun _ hx =>\n104\t  \u27e8closure_minimal Set.inter_subset_left d.isClosed_supportLocus hx.1, hx.2\u27e9\n105\t\n106\t/-- The support trace on an open is closed in the whole space iff nothing leaks. -/\n107\tlemma isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (U : X.Opens) :\n108\t    IsClosed (d.supportLocus \u2229 (U : Set X)) \u2194 d.supportLeak U = \u2205 := by\n109\t  constructor\n110\t  \u00b7 intro h\n111\t    rw [supportLeak, h.closure_eq, Set.sdiff_eq_empty]\n112\t    exact Set.inter_subset_right\n113\t  \u00b7 intro h\n114\t    rw [supportLeak, Set.sdiff_eq_empty] at h\n115\t    exact isClosed_of_closure_subset fun x hx =>\n116\t      \u27e8closure_minimal Set.inter_subset_left d.isClosed_supportLocus hx, h hx\u27e9\n117\t\n118\t/-- **The fibre no-leak criterion** \u2014 the named threading slot for the fibrewise data\n119\tof the (c1)-finite clause: if over every base point the fibre of the closure of the\n120\ttrace stays inside `U`, the leak locus is empty.  In the CertUniv instantiation the\n121\thypothesis is produced from the seed design and the P-fib-N fibre analysis (the fibre\n122\tsupport is a finite set of pairwise-incomparable closed points, each isolated inside\n123\tits piece). -/\n124\tlemma supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre (f : X \u27f6 S) {U : X.Opens}\n125\t    (hfib : \u2200 s : S, f.base \u207b\u00b9' {s} \u2229 closure (d.supportLocus \u2229 (U : Set X))\n126\t      \u2286 (U : Set X)) :\n127\t    d.supportLeak U = \u2205 := by\n128\t  rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]\n129\t  rintro x \u27e8hxc, hxU\u27e9\n130\t  exact hxU (hfib (f.base x) \u27e8rfl, hxc\u27e9)\n131\t\n132\t/-- **The base image of the leak locus is closed** under a universally closed morphism\n133\t(the properness licence): its complement is the Zariski-open locus of the base over\n134\twhich the support trace on `U` is closed \u2014 the tube-side mechanism for producing the\n135\tclosed-trace input Zariski-locally on the base.    240	  \prod_{(i,j)} Q_{ij}\) be the two restriction maps, \(\delta^-\) restricting the
   241	  \(i\)-component and \(\delta^+\) the \(j\)-component. The \emph{glued colength module} is
   242	  their equalizer
   243	  \[
   244	    W(A) \;:=\; \ker\bigl(\delta^- - \delta^+\bigr) \;\subseteq\; \prod_j Q_j ,
   245	  \]
   246	  an \(R\)-submodule; concretely \(s \in W(A)\) iff \(s_i\) and \(s_j\) have the same image
   247	  in \(Q_{ij}\) for every pair \((i,j)\). It is the module of global sections of the
   248	  structure sheaf of the divisor over the union of the pieces.
