   251	\begin{definition}[The colength certificate of degree \(n\)]
   252	  \label{def:isCertified}
   253	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified}
   254	  \uses{def:gluedColength}
   255	  \leanok
   256	  \source{kleiman-picard}
   257	  A finite chart adaptation \(A\) is \emph{certified of degree \(n\)} if
   258	  \begin{enumerate}
   259	    \item[(c1)] every chart colength module \(Q_j\) is finite and projective over \(R\);
   260	    \item[(c2)] the glued colength module \(W(A)\) is finite and projective over \(R\), and
   261	      has constant rank \(n\) at every prime: \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathfrak p} W(A) = n\)
   262	      for all \(\mathfrak p \in \Spec R\);
   263	    \item[(c3)] the cokernel of the inclusion \(W(A) \hookrightarrow \prod_j Q_j\) is flat
   264	      over \(R\);
   265	    \item[(c4)] the cokernel of \(\delta^- - \delta^+\) is flat over \(R\).
   266	  \end{enumerate}
   267	  Clauses (c1) and (c2) say that the divisor is finite flat of degree \(n\) over the base
   268	  --- Kleiman's condition that a relative effective divisor of degree \(n\) have
   269	  \(S\)-flat structure sheaf with fibres of length \(n\). Clauses (c3) and (c4) are what

   272	  \(0 \to W(A) \to \prod_j Q_j \to \prod_{ij} Q_{ij}\) with \(R'\) stays exact, so that the

   285	  A \emph{certified divisor family of degree \(n\)} over \(R\) is a triple \((d, A, c)\):

   308	\section{The Zariski-local certificate}
   309	\label{sec:divfamzar}

   311	The certificate of \ref{def:isCertified} is a condition on \emph{global} modules over
   312	\(R\), and it is genuinely restrictive: it forces the divisor to sit, chart-trace by
   313	chart-trace, in a closed way inside the two pinned charts. The next theorem is that
   314	obstruction, and it is the reason the functor of Section~\ref{sec:divfam} is not the one

   317	\begin{theorem}[The chart obstruction to a global certificate]
   318	  \label{thm:isCertified_chart_obstruction}

   900	    AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.equiv,

332:{"kind": "tool_result", "at": "2026-07-31T08:06:04.345497+00:00", "text": "", "tool": "Bash", "data": {"content": "     1	\chapter{The divisor scheme and the representability of \(\mathrm{Pic}^0\)}
     2	\label{chap:DivisorScheme}
     3	
     4	Grothendieck's construction of the Picard scheme does not represent \(\mathrm{Pic}\)
     5	directly. It represents first the functor of relative effective divisors, and then
     6	presents \(\mathrm{Pic}\) as a quotient of that divisor scheme along the Abel map: the
     7	Abel map is a surjection of sheaves whose fibres are linear systems, and a scheme
     8	representing \(\mathrm{Pic}\) is obtained by descending along it
     9	(\ref{def:localEquations_picClass}, and Kleiman's Theorem 4.8 and its proof).
    10	
    11	This chapter builds the divisor half of that argument for the curve \(C/k\) of
    12	Chapter~\ref{chap:Challenge}, in the form in which the representability seam
    13	\ref{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts} can consume it. The three steps are:
    14	
    15	\begin{enumerate}
    16	  \item a functor \(\Div^{\,n}_{C/k}\) of degree-\(n\) relative divisors, defined on affine
    17	    test algebras by \emph{local equations plus a finite chart adaptation carrying a
    18	    colength certificate}, and its Zariski-localised form (Sections
    19	    \ref{sec:divfam}--\ref{sec:divfamzar});
    20	  \item an embedding \(\varepsilon\) of that functor into a product of two Grassmannians,
    21	    sending a divisor \(D\) to the pair of window submodules
    22	    \(H^0(\OO(aF - D)) \subseteq H^0(\OO(aF))\) at two pinned exponents \(a\), and a closed
    23	    subscheme \(\mathbf{Div}\) of that Grassmannian pair carved out by the multiplication
    24	    condition which the image satisfies (Section~\ref{sec:divscheme}); this is
    25	    Grothendieck's embedding of a Quot-type functor into a Grassmannian by a twisted
    26	    pushforward;
    27	  \item the \emph{backward} half of representability --- every divisor class over an affine
    28	    test induces a unique morphism to \(\mathbf{Div}\), and the class is recoverable from
    29	    that morphism (Section~\ref{sec:divclassify}).
    30	\end{enumerate}
    31	
    32	The forward half --- a universal divisor family on \(\mathbf{Div}\) --- is not built here.
    33	Section~\ref{sec:divrep} states exactly what it must be, derives the affine equivalence and
    34	the chart family of \ref{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts} from it, and isolates the
    35	unproved statement (\ref{thm:divRepUniversalFamily}).
    36	
    37	Throughout, \(k\) is a field, \(C\) is a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over
    38	\(k\) of genus \(g\), \(\pi \colon C \to \PP^1_k\) is a finite dominant morphism, and
    39	\(F\) is its fibre Weil divisor (\ref{def:fiberWeilDivisor}). For a \(k\)-algebra \(R\) we
    40	write \(C_R\) for the relative curve (\ref{def:relCurve}) and \(V_0^R, V_1^R\) for the two
    41	pinned charts of \(C_R\) obtained by pulling back the two standard charts of \(\PP^1\)
    42	along \(\pi\) (\ref{def:relCover}, \ref{def:fiberTwoCover}). We abbreviate
    43	\(H_a := H^0(C, \OO(aF))\) (\ref{def:divisorSections}).
    44	
    45	\section{Divisor equality of local-equation systems}
   118	\section{The relative divisor functor of the curve}
   119	\label{sec:divfam}
   120	
   121	Fix a \(k\)-algebra \(R\). A relative effective divisor on \(C_R/R\) is, locally on
   122	\(C_R\), cut out by one equation which is regular on the fibres; a local-equation system on
   123	\(C_R\) records exactly that, but on an \emph{arbitrary} pointed cover, and with regularity
   124	asked in the stalks of \(C_R\) rather than on the fibres. Two further data turn a
   125	local-equation system into a value of a functor with a finite presentation: a refinement of
   126	its cover by finitely many basic opens of the two pinned charts, and a certificate
   127	asserting that the resulting colength modules are finite projective over \(R\) of constant
   128	rank \(n\). The certificate is what plays the role of \(R\)-flatness with fibres of degree
   129	\(n\) in Kleiman's Definition of \(\Div^{\,n}_{X/S}\).
   130	
   131	\begin{definition}[Finite chart cover data]
   132	  \label{def:finCoverData}
   133	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData, AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.pieces,
   134	    AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.cover₀, AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.cover₁,
   135	    AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.isAffineOpen_pieces,
   136	    AlgebraicGeometry.le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one}
   137	  \uses{def:relCurve, def:relCover, def:fiberTwoCover}
   138	  \leanok
   139	  \emph{Finite chart cover data} on \(C_R\) consists of finitely many sections
   140	  \(h^0_1,\dots,h^0_{m_0} \in \struct{}(V_0^R)\) and \(h^1_1,\dots,h^1_{m_1} \in
   141	  \struct{}(V_1^R)\), together with coefficients \(a^\iota_j\) in the same rings satisfying
   142	  the two partition identities
   143	  \[
   144	    \sum_{j} a^0_j h^0_j = 1 \ \text{ in } \struct{}(V_0^R), \qquad
   145	    \sum_{j} a^1_j h^1_j = 1 \ \text{ in } \struct{}(V_1^R).
   146	  \]
   147	  Its \emph{pieces} are the basic opens \(P_j := D(h^\iota_j) \subseteq V_\iota^R\), indexed
   148	  by the disjoint union of the two index sets. Each piece is affine, and the pieces of each
   149	  chart cover that chart:
   150	  \(V_0^R = \bigcup_j D(h^0_j)\) and \(V_1^R = \bigcup_j D(h^1_j)\).
   151	\end{definition}
   152	\begin{proof}
   153	  \leanok
   154	  A basic open of an affine open is affine, and the pinned charts are affine over the
   155	  base, so each \(P_j\) is affine.
   156	
   157	  For the covering claim on \(V_0^R\): let \(z \in V_0^R\) and suppose \(z \notin D(h^0_j)\)
   158	  for every \(j\), that is, the germ of every \(h^0_j\) at \(z\) lies in the maximal ideal
   159	  of \(\struct{C_R, z}\). Taking germs at \(z\) in the partition identity gives
   160	  \(1 = \sum_j (a^0_j)_z (h^0_j)_z\), which exhibits \(1\) as an element of the maximal
   161	  ideal --- impossible in a local ring. Hence some \(h^0_j\) is a unit at \(z\), i.e.\
   162	  \(z \in D(h^0_j)\). The same argument applies on \(V_1^R\).
   163	\end{proof}

   165	\begin{definition}[Finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system]
   166	  \label{def:divisorAdaptation}
   167	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation, AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors}

   171	  Let \(d\) be a local-equation system on \(C_R\), adapted to a pointed cover
   172	  \(\mathcal U\). A \emph{finite chart adaptation} \(A\) of \(d\) consists of finite chart
   173	  cover data (\ref{def:finCoverData}) with pieces \(P_j\), together with sections
   174	  \(f_j \in \struct{}(P_j)\) subject to the \emph{refinement clause}: for every piece index
   175	  \(j\) and every point \(y \in C_R\) there is a unit
   176	  \(u \in \struct{}(P_j \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times}\) with
   177	  \[
   178	    f_j\big|_{P_j \cap \mathcal U(y)} \;=\; u \cdot d_y\big|_{P_j \cap \mathcal U(y)} .
   179	  \]
   180	  (The quantifier ranges over \emph{all} \(y\); over an empty overlap the section ring is
   180	  (The quantifier ranges over \emph{all} \(y\); over an empty overlap the section ring is
   181	  the zero ring and the clause is vacuous.)

   184	  given a point \(p_j\) with \(P_j \subseteq \mathcal U(p_j)\) and a unit \(w_j\) on
   185	  \(P_j\) with \(f_j = w_j \cdot d_{p_j}|_{P_j}\), then the refinement clause holds for
   186	  every \(y\), with unit the product of \(w_j|\) and the restriction of the transition unit
   187	  \(g_{p_j y}\) of \(d\) (\ref{lem:localEquations_ratioUnit}).

   192	  to \(W := P_j \cap \mathcal U(y)\). Restricting \(f_j = w_j\, d_{p_j}|_{P_j}\) to \(W\)

   194	  transition unit, \(d_{p_j}|_{\mathcal U(p_j) \cap \mathcal U(y)} = g_{p_j y}\,

   201	\begin{lemma}[The adapted equations are regular]
   202	  \label{lem:divisorAdaptation_eqn_regular}
   203	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular}
   204	  \uses{def:divisorAdaptation, def:localEquations}
   205	  \leanok
   206	  Let \(A\) be a finite chart adaptation of \(d\). For every piece index \(j\) and every
   207	  point \(z \in P_j\), the germ of \(f_j\) at \(z\) is a nonzerodivisor in
   208	  \(\struct{C_R,z}\).

   213	  point \(y := z\) itself. The point \(z\) lies in \(P_j\) and in \(\mathcal U(z)\), hence
   214	  in the overlap \(W := P_j \cap \mathcal U(z)\), so germs at \(z\) may be taken in the
   215	  identity \(f_j|_W = u\, d_z|_W\); germs commute with restriction, so
   216	  \[

   224	\begin{definition}[The chart colength modules and their glued equalizer]
   225	  \label{def:gluedColength}
   226	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.colength,
   227	    AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.ovlColength,
   228	    AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule,
   229	    AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.mem_gluedSubmodule_iff}
   230	  \uses{def:divisorAdaptation, lem:divisorAdaptation_eqn_regular}
   231	  \leanok
   232	  Let \(A\) be a finite chart adaptation of \(d\), with pieces \(P_j\) and equations

     1	\chapter{The Jacobian datum}
     2	\label{chap:Jacobian}
     3	
     4	Throughout this chapter \(k\) is a field and \(C\) is the challenge curve: a
     5	scheme over \(k\), proper, smooth of relative dimension one, and geometrically
     6	irreducible. The degree-zero relative Picard functor
     7	\(\Pic^0_{C/k} : \Over(\Spec k)^{\op} \to \mathrm{CommGrp}\) was constructed in
     8	\ref{def:pic0Functor}. This chapter introduces the \emph{Jacobian datum} --- a
     9	representing object for \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) together with the certificates its
    10	construction provides --- and develops what follows formally from it: the
    11	group structure and universal property of the representing object, its
    12	uniqueness up to canonical isomorphism, separatedness (every group scheme over
    13	a field is separated), the homogeneity supplied by translations, and, given a
    14	proper irreducible \emph{Abel source} mapping onto it, properness and geometric
    15	irreducibility.

    AJCR: characterize theta-ideal range germwise
    
    On every open, the theta-ideal inclusion range is now iff germwise divisor vanishing of both pinned components.
    Archon-Run: 0100
    Archon-Round: 1
    Archon-Role: horizon
    Archon-Session: 0004-horizon-pic-d

diff --git a/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorThetaSheafSequence.lean b/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorThetaSheafSequence.lean
index 9084e48fef..cf01617256 100644
--- a/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorThetaSheafSequence.lean
+++ b/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorThetaSheafSequence.lean
@@ -453,6 +453,33 @@ theorem exists_thetaIdealInclApp_of_germ_mem
       twistRes R V₀ V₁ (relThetaCocycle C R π a) (hUW true) x
     rw [show secRes ((A.thetaIdealDatum a).sheaf) (hUW true) σ = s true from hσ true]
     exact hlocal true
+
+/-- The pointwise range of the theta-ideal inclusion on an arbitrary open is exactly
+the theta sections whose two pinned components vanish along the divisor germwise. -/
+theorem mem_range_thetaIdealInclApp_iff_germ_mem
+    {W : (relCurve C R).Opens}
+    (x : (relThetaTwistSheaf C R π a).obj.obj (op W)) :
+    x ∈ LinearMap.range (A.thetaIdealInclApp (a := a) W) ↔
+      (∀ (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ W ⊓
+        (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀),
+        ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (W ⊓
+          (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀) z hz).hom x.val.1 ∈ d.stalkIdeal z) ∧
+      (∀ (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ W ⊓
+        (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁),
+        ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (W ⊓
+          (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁) z hz).hom x.val.2 ∈ d.stalkIdeal z) := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
+    constructor
+    · intro z hz
+      exact germ_gluedToIdeal₀_mem (A := A) (a := a) inf_le_right
+        (secRes ((A.thetaIdealDatum a).sheaf) inf_le_left s) z hz
+    · intro z hz
+      exact germ_gluedToIdeal₁_mem (A := A) (a := a) inf_le_right
+        (secRes ((A.thetaIdealDatum a).sheaf) inf_le_left s) z hz
+  · rintro ⟨hx0, hx1⟩
+    obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := A.exists_thetaIdealInclApp_of_germ_mem (a := a) x hx0 hx1
+    exact ⟨s, hs⟩
 /-! ## Global right exactness -/
 
 /-- Vanishing of `H^1(O(a Theta - d))` makes the theta quotient sheaf globally generated

ADVANCED, NO GATE CLOSED (ajcr-p1, run 0087 r0+r1).

WHY THE ROW EXISTS. IsChartUniv (antecedent 1 of pic0RepresentableByOfCharts, Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) had exactly TWO routes and BOTH pass through the UNRESTRICTED certificate three headers call false. r0 landed the repair: RestrictedChartFibre + isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre (Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean, commits fe937438c/5439077ad/2327a0757).

r1 SETTLED THE INHABITATION QUESTION r0 LEFT OPEN, and r0's pricing of it was FALSE. Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean, 10 declarations, sorry-free, lake build EXIT=0 (8893 jobs), ALL axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] vs a control firing sorryAx.
 * restrictedChartFibre_bot -- the class IS INHABITED at V = bot, unconditionally. r0 called the obstruction 'triviality of picEt over the empty scheme: a genuinely separate lemma, absent from the tree'. It is Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover + Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology, both mathlib, three lines. The error was the REDUCTION (a congr 1 discarding that pic0SigmaSheaf is a SHEAF), not the census. I-0890 retracted at its site.
 * isChartUniv_bot -- so antecedent 1 is FREE at V = bot, with no hypothesis. And isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart_bot shows the construction never mentions the Abel chart: it holds for an ARBITRARY map into the Sigma-sheaf. A route reaching IsChartUniv without pinning V proves nothing about the chart.
 * not_coverageContainment_bot -- coverage's containment is FALSE at bot whenever a test has a point.
 * At the other end: range_subset_range_top_iota (containment free at top) and isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_restrictedChartFibre_top (hf at top RETURNS the unrestricted certificate). not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective refutes top outright, conditional on p3's abel-noninj fork.

*** TWO THINGS TO CARRY OFF THIS ROW.

     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Canonical cocycles of representability isomorphisms
    10	
    11	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso` is defined by Yoneda uniqueness, but mathlib does
    12	not expose the two equations that descent data consume: its universal-element intertwining
    13	formula and transitivity for three independently chosen representing objects.  These generic
    14	lemmas make those equations explicit.  In particular, the transitivity theorem proves a
    15	three-face cocycle without defining the `1,3` face as a composite.
    16	-/

    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe v u
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory
    23	
    24	namespace CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy
    25	
    26	/-- Composition with the canonical representing-object isomorphism transports the universal
    27	element unchanged. -/
    28	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    29	    {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : C} (e : F.RepresentableBy Y)
    30	    (e' : F.RepresentableBy Y') {X : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    31	    e'.homEquiv (f ≫ (e.uniqueUpToIso e').hom) = e.homEquiv f := by
    32	  have h : (e.uniqueUpToIso e').hom =
    33	      e'.homEquiv.symm (e.homEquiv (𝟙 Y)) := rfl
    34	  rw [h, comp_homEquiv_symm, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    35	  rw [← e.homEquiv_comp f (𝟙 Y), Category.comp_id]
    36	
    37	/-- The canonical isomorphisms between three representations satisfy the cocycle law.  The
    38	`1,3` comparison is the independently defined `uniqueUpToIso e₁ e₃`, not a composite alias. -/
    39	theorem uniqueUpToIso_trans {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    40	    {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y₁ Y₂ Y₃ : C}
    41	    (e₁ : F.RepresentableBy Y₁) (e₂ : F.RepresentableBy Y₂)
    42	    (e₃ : F.RepresentableBy Y₃) :
    43	    e₁.uniqueUpToIso e₃ = e₁.uniqueUpToIso e₂ ≪≫ e₂.uniqueUpToIso e₃ := by
    44	  apply Iso.ext
    45	  apply e₃.homEquiv.injective
    46	  calc
    47	    e₃.homEquiv (e₁.uniqueUpToIso e₃).hom = e₁.homEquiv (𝟙 Y₁) := by
